newsitem.title: ITALY: Comit declines comment on BankNapoli.
newsitem.headline: Comit declines comment on BankNapoli.

text.p: Banca Commerciale Italiana Managing Director Luigi Fausti said on Wednesday that the rescue of Banco di Napoli was of concern to all banks but declined to comment directly on whether he was interested in bidding.
"We haven't discussed it yet," Fausti told reporters after a meeting of the Italian Banking Association (ABI).

The Treasury has announced plans to sell off an initial 60 percent of the bank, which unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year.
Ambroveneto is the only group so far to express an interest in bidding for Banco di Napoli but analysts believe Banca Comerciale might also be keen.
"I think sorting out Banco di Napoli is of interest to all banks because it is a destabilising factor, it's a general problem," Fausti told reporters.
Sandro Molinari, chairman of Cariplo said his group "is not interested" in Banco di Napoli and Alfonzo Iozzo, managing director of San Paolo, said he "would not take part" in the auction.
A source from BNL said that bank "thought it very unlikely" it would take part.
